answer: Medicare Part D covers Viagra-type drugs when prescribed for an FDA-approved use other than sexual or erectile dysfunction, such as pulmonary hypertension, but not when used off-label. The passages do not state Florida Medicaid's rule for these drugs.

citations.quote: ED drugs will meet the definition of a Part D drug when prescribed for medically accepted indications approved by the FDA other than sexual or erectile dysfunction such as pulmonary hypertension.
However, ED drugs will not meet the definition of a Part D drug when used off-label, even if the off label use is listed in one of the compendia found in section 1927(g)(1)(B)(i) of the Act.

gold_answer: Both can. Florida Medicaid excludes erectile dysfunction drugs unless prescribed for another FDA-approved condition, and Part D treats ED drugs as covered Part D drugs when prescribed for an FDA-approved indication other than sexual or erectile dysfunction, such as pulmonary hypertension.
gold_quote: Erectile dysfunction drugs, unless prescribed for a condition other than sexual or erectile dysfunction as approved by the U.S. FDA || ED drugs will meet the definition of a Part D drug when prescribed for medically-accepted indications approved by the FDA other than sexual or erectile dysfunction (such as pulmonary hypertension).

judge.rationale: The answer correctly describes Part D coverage of ED drugs for FDA-approved non-ED indications, but it says the Florida Medicaid rule is not covered and so misses half of the gold answer, while all of its claims appear in the cited passage.

question: Will either Florida Medicaid or Medicare Part D pay for Viagra-type pills if my doctor prescribes them for something other than erection problems?
